acceptanceCriteria.criterion: API keys are cryptographically strong (256-bit, 32 bytes from crypto.randomBytes)
API keys are stored as SHA-256 hashes in the database (not plaintext)
Database table api_keys stores: id (cuid), keyHash (unique), name, createdAt, revokedAt (nullable)
Admin endpoint POST /api/v1/admin/keys with body {"name": "string"} generates new API key and returns plaintext key ONCE in response
Admin endpoint DELETE /api/v1/admin/keys/:id sets revokedAt timestamp (soft delete)
Authentication plugin validates Bearer token in Authorization header against stored hashes
Invalid or revoked keys return 401 Unauthorized with structured error response containing code "UNAUTHORIZED"
Rate limiting enforced at configurable requests per hour per API key via @fastify/rate-limit (default: 100/hour)
Request exceeding rate limit returns 429 Rate Limit Exceeded with Retry-After header
Authenticated requests include API key ID in request context (request.apiKeyId) for downstream use

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: System SHALL issue API keys for webhook ingestion with key rotation, revocation capability, and rate limiting per key.

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: API keys SHALL be cryptographically strong (256-bit minimum), stored as salted hashes (bcrypt or Argon2), support key rotation without service disruption, and rate limiting per key to prevent abuse.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Generate new API key using randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'), store SHA-256 hash using createHash('sha256'), return plaintext key ONCE. validateKey() hashes input and queries database.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Configure @fastify/rate-limit with max: 100 requests per timeWindow: '1 hour', keyGenerator extracts API key from Authorization header, custom errorResponseBuilder for structured 429 response.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Services use pattern: api-key.service.ts. Routes: specs.route.ts. Plugins: rate-limit.ts. Database columns: camelCase (keyHash, createdAt). REST API: plural nouns with /api/v1/ prefix.

doc.title: Technical Specification Epic 1
doc.snippet: API keys cryptographically strong (256-bit random tokens), stored as SHA-256 hashes, admin endpoints for key generation and revocation, authentication middleware validates Bearer token, rate limiting per API key.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.snippet: Role: Backend Developer. Action: API key generation, storage, and validation middleware. Benefit: Only authorized services can upload API specs. Includes admin endpoints, auth middleware, rate limiting.

artifact.reason: Main Fastify application setup. Register new auth and rate-limit plugins here. Error handler already supports UNAUTHORIZED (401) and RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (429) codes. setNotFoundHandler pattern established.
Singleton Prisma client pattern. Use DatabaseService.getInstance() for database queries in api-key.service.ts. Follow same singleton export pattern.
Environment variable validation pattern. Add RATE_LIMIT_MAX to EnvironmentConfig interface. Follow same optional vs required pattern.
Add ApiKey model here. pgvector extension already enabled. Follow cuid() id pattern and DateTime defaults.
Integration test pattern using app.inject(). Follow same beforeAll/afterAll setup with buildApp(). Error response structure validated at lines 84-98. Use this pattern for auth and rate limit tests.
Test setup with dotenv and DatabaseService initialization. Tests use real database connection.

constraints.constraint: API keys MUST be 256-bit (32 bytes) minimum per NFR-SEC1
Keys stored as SHA-256 hashes only, never plaintext in database
Plaintext key returned ONCE during creation, never retrievable afterward
Rate limiting default 100 requests/hour, configurable via RATE_LIMIT_MAX environment variable
Authentication uses Fastify plugin pattern with onRequest hook and decorateRequest (not Express-style middleware)
Error responses follow structured format: { error: { code, message, details? } }
Services follow singleton pattern like DatabaseService
Integration tests use app.inject() pattern with real database

interface.name: POST /api/v1/admin/keys
DELETE /api/v1/admin/keys/:id
interface.signature: Response 204: No Content Error 404: { error: { code: "NOT_FOUND", message: string } }

interface.name: ApiKeyService
interface.signature: generateApiKey(): string hashApiKey(key: string): string createApiKey(name: string): Promise<{ id: string, key: string, name: string, createdAt: Date }> revokeApiKey(id: string): Promise<void> validateApiKey(key: string): Promise<{ id: string } | null>

interface.name: authPlugin
interface.signature: Decorates: request.apiKeyId (string | null) Hook: onRequest - validates Bearer token Returns: 401 if invalid, continues if valid

interface.name: rateLimitPlugin
interface.signature: Config: { max: number, timeWindow: '1 hour', keyGenerator: Function } Returns: 429 with Retry-After header when limit exceeded

tests.standards: Vitest is the testing framework with @vitest/ui for visual test runner. Tests use real database connections via Prisma. Integration tests use Fastify's app.inject() method for HTTP request simulation without starting the server. Test files follow *.test.ts pattern in src/__tests__/ directory. Setup file initializes DatabaseService before tests and disconnects after. Tests validate both success responses and standardized error structures. Environment variables loaded from .env file via dotenv/config.
